A.explanation: Moments calculated about different points cannot be equated, so saying clockwise about one point equals anticlockwise about a different arbitrary point is not valid.

B.explanation: The centre of gravity is only one possible point and the principle holds for any point, not only the centre of gravity.

C.explanation: The pivot is only one possible point and many objects in rotational equilibrium have no physical pivot.

D.explanation: For zero resultant moment, clockwise and anticlockwise moments must be calculated about the same reference point so their perpendicular distances are consistent.

hints: Notice the statement starts with clockwise moments about any point - the missing words must tell you which point to use for the anticlockwise moments.
Recall that a moment $moment = F \times d$ depends on the perpendicular distance $d$ from the line of force to the chosen point.
A clockwise total and an anticlockwise total can only cancel to give zero resultant moment if both totals use the same distances from the same reference point.
walkthrough: Identify the given condition: the object is in rotational equilibrium, so resultant moment is zero and clockwise effects must balance anticlockwise effects.
State the physical rule: moment of a force depends on the point it is calculated about, because $moment = force \times perpendicular distance$ from that point.
Explain the comparison: changing the reference point changes each distance and therefore changes each moment, so totals about two different points are not directly comparable.
Conclude that both sums must be taken about one common point for the equality to mean zero net turning effect.
That wording is completed by the same point. This is option D.
